chunk_list: ARIADNA QUESTION ANNOTATION GUIDE V1.1 1. Purpose This guide defines how bilingual questions in the ARIADNA benchmark are created, classified, reviewed, and adjudicated. Version 1.1 incorporates revised criteria for temporal questions, multi-hop questions, version comparisons, and unanswerable cases following the reopening of the corpus. Every semantic question has one Spanish and one English version. Both share the intent, category, difficulty, reference answer, required facts, sources, citations, relevant date, and adjudication decision. Wording must be natural in each language and must not be a mechanical translation revealing answer terms. 2. Principles Questions must be answerable using the corpus alone. External knowledge, speculative inference, and subjective preference are not permitted. Difficulty must arise from locating, relating, and understanding evidence rather than deliberately confusing wording. A question remains grouped with its translations, paraphrases, and variants sharing an answer or essential evidence. This grouping prevents leakage across training, development, and test. Split assignment occurs after semantic groups are formed. Superseded sources remain available for historical questions. A question about the current state uses the version valid at the freeze date.

File creation or modification dates do not replace the validity period where the two differ. 3. Annotation structure The record contains an identifier, languages, question, intent, category, difficulty, reference date, answer, atomic facts, primary sources, alternative sources, citations, required relations, status, and comments. Every field has a defined vocabulary or format. The reference answer does not impose one exact wording. It defines the facts a valid answer must contain and the conditions preventing an answer. Citations must cover every required fact and use the appropriate version. Annotation criterion 1 Category 1, direct, is used where the main answer appears as an explicit assertion in one source. The annotator must justify the category and discard close alternatives. A question is not classified by the number of documents retrieved by a system but by the evidence required in the corpus. ES/EN pairs always receive the same category and equivalent sources.

Uncertain cases enter adjudication and do not enter the official split until resolved. Annotation criterion 2 Category 2, temporal, is used where the answer depends on a date, validity period, sequence, or status change. The annotator must justify the category and discard close alternatives. A question is not classified by the number of documents retrieved by a system but by the evidence required in the corpus. ES/EN pairs always receive the same category and equivalent sources. Uncertain cases enter adjudication and do not enter the official split until resolved. Annotation criterion 3 Category 3, multi-hop, is used where the answer requires combining at least two necessary facts. The annotator must justify the category and discard close alternatives. A question is not classified by the number of documents retrieved by a system but by the evidence required in the corpus. ES/EN pairs always receive the same category and equivalent sources.

Uncertain cases enter adjudication and do not enter the official split until resolved. Annotation criterion 4 Category 4, version comparison, is used where the question requests identification of a difference across versions. The annotator must justify the category and discard close alternatives. A question is not classified by the number of documents retrieved by a system but by the evidence required in the corpus. ES/EN pairs always receive the same category and equivalent sources. Uncertain cases enter adjudication and do not enter the official split until resolved. Annotation criterion 5 Category 5, unanswerable, is used where the corpus contains insufficient evidence for a reliable answer. The annotator must justify the category and discard close alternatives. A question is not classified by the number of documents retrieved by a system but by the evidence required in the corpus. ES/EN pairs always receive the same category and equivalent sources.

Uncertain cases enter adjudication and do not enter the official split until resolved. Annotation criterion 6 Temporal rule 1, current state, establishes that annotation uses the version current at the freeze date. The record stores the relevant time and the source proving validity. Where a rule announces a change not yet effective, the answer distinguishes the current state from the future modification. An email or document date is used only where it truly represents the event time. Previous_version and next_version relations are verified before approval. Annotation criterion 7 Temporal rule 2, historical state, establishes that annotation uses the source valid on the explicitly requested date. The record stores the relevant time and the source proving validity. Where a rule announces a change not yet effective, the answer distinguishes the current state from the future modification. An email or document date is used only where it truly represents the event time. Previous_version and next_version relations are verified before approval.

Annotation criterion 8 Temporal rule 3, change, establishes that annotation requires at least two states and the date or event of replacement. The record stores the relevant time and the source proving validity. Where a rule announces a change not yet effective, the answer distinguishes the current state from the future modification. An email or document date is used only where it truly represents the event time. Previous_version and next_version relations are verified before approval. Annotation criterion 12 Multi-hop rule 1, owner and deadline, requires the annotation to first identify the task and then its owner or date. Hops must be necessary and appear in the logical order of the answer. Where one source directly contains every fact, the question is not multi-hop even if related sources exist. Every hop links to a corpus identifier or relation. Connections based only on general knowledge or thematic similarity are not permitted. Annotation criterion 13 Multi-hop rule 2, proposal and approval, requires the annotation to distinguish who proposes a change and which source confirms it. Hops must be necessary and appear in the logical order of the answer. Where one source directly contains every fact, the question is not multi-hop even if related sources exist. Every hop links to a corpus identifier or relation. Connections based only on general knowledge or thematic similarity are not permitted. Every hop links to a corpus identifier or relation. Connections based only on general knowledge or thematic similarity are not permitted.

Every hop links to a corpus identifier or relation. Connections based only on general knowledge or thematic similarity are not permitted. A person other than the question author examines the record and complete source. Disagreements are recorded with the initial label, proposal, and final decision. Semantic changes are applied to both language versions. A question becomes approved only where no critical field remains pending and its citations can be located in the original artifacts.
